 A penalty from Harry Kane and additional goals from Ezri Konsa and Ben White – before Elliot Anderson was sent off – gave England a potentially epochal win

 9m ago 17.14 EST Righto, that’s it from us for now. England have ended Spain’s 43-game unbeaten run, the world and European champions beaten in their capital for the first time in 39 years – the oldies among us will recall Gary Lineker’s four-goal haul in white shirts, white shorts, white stockings.
 But this might just be a new England, one prepared to act as the protagonist against all opposition, in all situations. Though there’s still work to be done, tonight’s performance was that of a squad who, after self-inflicted suffering they’ll be rueing until they die, have said “No más”.
 Peace out.
 Share 17m ago 17.06 EST “Brilliant performance and a well-deserved win … from start to finish,” says Tuchel, who doesn’t understand why the penalty was also a red card; er, because there was no attempt to play the ball. 
 He says it was a deserved win, England focusing on their performance and attitude; he can’t praise the team highly enough and says “Against this team, half an hour feels like two hours.”
 Asked about Trafford, he doesn’t think he’s found a new no 1, but praises the double save as what he was there to do.
 Finally, he says they had their best World Cup in 60 years – not sure about that, given the quality of opportunity they spurned – weren’t happy with it, and that’s about it.
 Share 20m ago 17.02 EST Aha, David Hytner’s match report is here… 
 England fend off fiery Spain fightback after Anderson’s red to top Nations League group Read more Share 21m ago 17.02 EST Also going on, but perhaps not for much longer: Andreeva, perhaps in the process of becoming the best in the world, is serving for the match.
 WTA Finals final: Elina Svitolina v Mirra Andreeva – live Read more Share 25m ago 16.57 EST We just saw a little shot of the England players gathering after the second Spain goal; whatever they said – “This doesn’t happen again”, perhaps – it worked. There was a certainty in the way they saw out the game, no longer waiting to lose but seizing the win.
 Share 28m ago 16.55 EST “We knew we was gonna beat them!” says Rice, who extols England’s first 10 minutes as the best they’ve played. He reckons that, but for the red card, they’d have scored more, as Spain jumped more to leave space in behind.
 Otherwise, he talks about looking up at the scoreboard, seeing not long to go, and all the players vowing to do anything for the badge, emptying the tank, then ITV cut away from him to show the goals again.
 Share 30m ago 16.53 EST Results from elsewhere
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: The Guardian Share 32m ago 16.51 EST I bet the England players are feeling frustration amid the elation. That performance ought to have been in their locker when it really mattered, but perhaps they needed one final failure to accept the need to change their ways. They were a different team tonight, committed to proactivity, and though they were helped by De la Fuente’s team selection, they attacked the game before that could even take effect, the way they played the first few minutes setting a tone.
 Share 35m ago 16.48 EST FULL TIME: Spain 2-3 England
 England beat the world and European champions, who lose for the first time in 968 days. They top the group but, more than that, deliver a performance of style and spine against the best around. If they go on to win anything, they’ll tell stories about tonight, Ben White’s tackle and James Trafford’s double save immortalised.
 Share 37m ago 16.46 EST 90+3 min Balls into the box, repelled by England . This has been a rearguard of moxie, organisation, heart, focus, discipline – all the things they aren’t! They’re almost there!
 Share 38m ago 16.45 EST 90+1 min A gorgeous pick into into the box from Lamine, a kind of scoop-poke that finds Fermin; he swivels, shoots … and Trafford tips away, but the ball reaches Oyarzabal, who shoots … and, somehow, Trafford is up in time to tip away again, a wondrous double-save! Spain, though, keep at it and keep working it, Pedri thunking an effort form the edge … into Trafford’s midriff! England’s keeper saves them, and if they see this out, he and Ben White have announced themselves as international players tonight. Incredible behaviour!
 View image in fullscreen James Trafford and Ezri Konsa react to his double save. Photograph: Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images Share Updated at  16.58 EST 41m ago 16.41 EST 90 min Spain have four additional minutes to preserve an unbeaten record stretching back two-and-a-half years.
 Share 43m ago 16.40 EST 89 min Lamine crosses … and it’s a goalkick. England bring on Burn for the heroic Ben White, his goal the winner as things stand and his tackle on Lamine to preserve it just as important.
 Share 43m ago 16.39 EST 87 min “Even if England somehow scrape through this, the story of the night isn’t how excellent we were for first hour – which we bloody were – but how we managed to stuff/almost stuff it up again,” reckons Christopher Lee.
 “Disappointing because this could really have been a turning point for the story of these players and Thomas Tuchel’s England reign. Even if we win from here it’ll still be backs to the wall England scraping through rather than dominate England smash the world champions.”
 I respectfully disagree: if england see this out, they’ll have the best of both worlds: a dominant display against the hardest team to do that too, then a backs-to-the-wall rearguard.
 Share 45m ago 16.37 EST 86 min This, my mates, has been a proper game of association football. Lamine picks a dink into the box, chested off by Fermin – who, like Pedri, has made a difference – but Porro can only drill wide. If De la Fuente had gone with those three subs from the start, we might’ve seen a different contest.
 Share 46m ago 16.36 EST 85 min England are deeper than they’d want to be but Konsa brings them up to the edge then, when Williams skates around the outside, beating Rogers, his cross is nasty … but Porro dives to head wide.
 Share 48m ago 16.35 EST 84 min A brilliant pass from Pedri sets Lamine free art inside-left! Is this his moment?! It is not because, out of nowhere, Benjamin White launches into a precision challenge, taking all of the ball and none of the man. That might be the tackle of his life, and could well be crucial.
 Share Updated at  16.40 EST 49m ago 16.33 EST 82 min Spain pass and England drop, but the supine resignation we saw against Argentina isn’t quite there. Changes for England: Spence and Calvert-Lewin for Bellingham and Gordon, which the Madrid man loves just as much as you’d expect.
 Share 51m ago 16.32 EST 80 min England are pinned back, too deep – we may have seen this one before. This time, instead of looking to commit a defeder, Lamine waves a low curler from edge, which Trafford dives to fist away – back into play, not around the post. But when the ball comes back, he gets it behind, and the corner comes to nowt.
 Share 53m ago 16.30 EST 79 min Spain are getting Lamine on the ball now and he teases Hall, who does really well not to buy what’s being sold, eventually blocking his man off with help from Trafford, and England clear.
 Share 54m ago 16.29 EST 78 min There’s such tempo and intensity to this game, and Tuchel acts, taking off Kane and introducing Lewis-Skelly. I can see why he’s done that but, on this occasion, I might’ve kept Kane on as a target man to hold the ball; who is the striker now?
 Share 55m ago 16.27 EST 77 min A bit of England possession, Gordon and Bellingham doing well in the inside-left channel, but this time when Bellingham crosses the ball soars behind for a goalkick.
 Share 1h ago 16.26 EST GOAL! Spain 2-3 England (Williams 75)
 How will England eff it up? Like this. Gordon tarries in possession, Pedri robbing him, then a fantastic first-time pass from Fermin sends Lamine away down the left. His low cross is a delight, Williams arriving on to it without breaking stride, and he swishes a finish in off the near post. It’s a different game now!
 View image in fullscreen Spain's forward Nico Williams celebrates scoring his team's second goal. Photograph: Thomas Coex/AFP/Getty Images Share Updated at  16.32 EST 1h ago 16.25 EST 73 min Spain win a corner down the right which yields another from the left. This time it goes short and, when the ball is clipped to the far post, Belling ham opts to let it go but Oyarzabal is behind him, and when he forces the cut-back, Fermin shoots … and Trafford parries. Pressure is building…
 Share 1h ago 16.22 EST 72 min A further change for Spain , Williams replacing Zubimendi as De la Fuente goes for it.
 Share 1h ago 16.21 EST 70 min Spain find Lamine on the right side of the box, but his attempted curler is blocked at source. England have defended superbly so far, the penalty Spain’s first shot on target.
 Share 1h ago 16.20 EST 69 min This is a proper test for England; not one Tuchel will have wanted but perhaps one the team needs. If they can make it through this, so wind up dominating Spain with 11, then seeing them away with 10, they’ll end the evening a different side to the one which started it. Lose and – though it’ll hurt – they can blame individual error.
 Share Updated at  16.21 EST 1h ago 16.18 EST 67 min Someone on the England bench is booked, and I wonder if Tuchel contemplates a change. He needs keep an out-ball, but perhaps midfield control means he remove Rogers for, perhaps, Lewis-Skelly.
 Share 1h ago 16.16 EST GOAL! Spain 1-3 England (Oyarzabal pen 65)
 Oyarzabal ambles up, skips, and when Trafford dives left, he sweeps right. Hold on to your toupees, this is going to be a serious 25 minutes.
 View image in fullscreen Mikel Oyarzabal of Spain celebrates scoring. Photograph: David Ramos/UEFA/Getty Images Share Updated at  16.20 EST 1h ago 16.15 EST PENALTY TO SPAIN AND A RED CARD FOR ELLIOT ANDERSON!
 64 min That question, eh? How will England eff it up? Like thus: Quansah is mugged by Lamine, the first time England have been so caught, and when Baena sweeps him in, Anderson hauls him back, a rash call, and Spain have a route back into the game!
 View image in fullscreen Lamine Yamal of Spain is fouled in the penalty area by Elliot Anderson of England which resulted in a red card for Anderson. Photograph: Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images Share Updated at  16.20 EST 1h ago 16.13 EST 62 min “Are you Scotland in disguise?” sing the away end, a disbelieving Philip Cornwall back in touch BUT EXCUSE ME WHILE I INTERRUPT MYSELF ONCE MORE!
 Share 1h ago 16.12 EST 61 min Gordon, who’s having a fine night, win another corner, and England will fancy another here, but this time Rice’s floaty delivery is easily fielded by Simon.
 Share 1h ago 16.11 EST 60 min And what a moment of redemption that is for White. Jeered by his own fans after leaving the World Cp squad in 2022, he’s nicely reintegrated now, and that was the kind of finish you’d expect to see from Pedro Porro. That is some serious praise.
 Share 1h ago 16.09 EST GOAL! Spain 0-3 England (White 58)
 Kane across the face of the box to Bellingham, who caresses in behind for White! He takes a touch, narrowing the angle but forcing the keeper to move then, when Simon spreads himself, he picks a very deliberate finish through the keeper’s legs! This is a hiding!
 View image in fullscreen England's Ben White scores their side's third goal. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA Share Updated at  16.10 EST 1h ago 16.08 EST 57 min Spain haven’t lost for 43 games …and BUT EXCUSE ME WHILE I INTERRUPT MYSELF … THEY’RE GOING TO LOSE TONIGHT!
 Share 1h ago 16.07 EST 56 min Bellingham, whose good work won the corner from which England scored, wins another ion similar style, this time down the left, as we see footgge of the England goal, Tuchel on the touchline also applying brow to imaginary ball – that’s how much time and space Konsa had. This time, the corner comes to nowt.
 Share 1h ago 16.06 EST 54 min Minor Spain protests for a free-kick of some sort, but VAR isn’t interested. Konsa couldn’t have been freer, the question on everybody’s lips a familiar one: how will they eff it up from here?
 Share 1h ago 16.04 EST GOAL! Spain 0-2 England (Konsa 53)
 A Rice outswinger and, in the middle of the box, Konsa has maybe five yards of space all around him to run in and guide home from seven yards. England are all over this!
 View image in fullscreen Ezri Konsa of England scores his team’s second goal. Photograph: Carl Recine/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Konsa celebrates scoring his team’s second goal. Photograph: Michael Regan/The FA/Getty Images Share Updated at  16.05 EST 1h ago 16.03 EST 52 min Zubimendi picks up a poor pass and punches between Anderosn and Rice, finding Lamine … whose trivela cross is straight at Trafford. Then England find Bellingham down the right of the box and he delays well before winning a corner off Pedri, gesticulating to where he thinks the away end is, but isn’t.
 Share 1h ago 16.01 EST 51 min Down the right, 30 yards from goal, Rice will swing the free-kick out … and Huijsen heads away well, facing his own goal.
 Share 1h ago 16.00 EST 49 min Lamine spreads wide to Cucurella, then Spain work it back to him, Hall delaying before Gordon confiscates possession. Those two have been brilliant so far and, when England counter, Rogers cuts inside Cucurella, who trips him and is booked.
 Share 1h ago 15.59 EST 48 min England win it high and win a throw, Tuchel’s alacrity in returning the ball evidencing their intent to speed up the game and impose their will. Spain soon have possession back, but it’s a message not to retreat.
 Share 1h ago 15.58 EST 48 min Already, Spain look calmer, Pedri linking play and finding pockets. England will, as Tuchel warned, have to be patient.
 Share 1h ago 15.56 EST 47 min “As I’m sure 347 other people are also pointing out,” chortles Bob O’Hara, “Pochettino made a pretty big managerial eff-up this week.”
 I fear that lush mane is on borrowed time – on which point is it just me who sees Stan Rizzo from Mad Men?
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: PR Company Handout Share 1h ago 15.56 EST 46 min We go again, those Spain changes reflecting England’s superiority.
 Share 1h ago 15.55 EST A triple Spain change: Huijsen, Pedri and Fermin on; Ruiz, Cubarsi and Merino off.
 Share 1h ago 15.54 EST Back come our teams… 
 Share 1h ago 15.53 EST Elsewhere, France are level at 0-0 playing Turkey in Bordeaux; Belgium have come from 1-0 down to lead Italy 3-1. As it stands, it’ll be France and Belgium moving on, Italy’s renaissance curtailed.
 Share 2h ago 15.52 EST “Benitez, Robbie Fowler’s last game for Liverpool,” writes Paul Oakes . “Takes him off with five minutes to go. Liverpool get a penalty one minute later.”
 I guess the idea was right, though – a proper reception.
 Share 2h ago 15.50 EST “What did Ferguson do against Chelsea in 2010?” asks Joshua Keeling. In a game United needed to not lose, he picked Nevlle, Giggs and Scholes, though younger, harder-running players had excelled against Bayern the previous midweek, United lost the game, lost the title, and lost the chance of four in a row.
 Share 2h ago 15.46 EST I wonder if De la Fuente will move to Pedri; the control we expect from Spain isn’t there tonight, and his ability to tempo-set might change this game. So far, Merino has been a cone, and it’s no great surprise; he’s a late-doors player, one who finds a goal when you’re desperate for one, rather than someone who gets involved in general play.
